text:
maria: quick note — hit a weird race on staging when a tenant eviction kicked off while an async migrate was in-flight. request ended up double-freeing a host page. repro fairly reliably under stress (concurrent tiny allocations).

sam: ugh. which code path? async offload or staged-mmap path?

maria: async migrate path (the one that copies pages to host then marks resident=false). i think the problem is the caller frees the slab while the migrate completion callback runs.

jung: do we have a short repro/log? any stack?

maria: pasted the short repro log:
```
E 03:44:22.123 evictor: mark_for_migrate page=0x7f8c... tenant=t-42
I 03:44:22.128 migrate: queued async migration token=tok-111
I 03:44:22.129 alloc: free slab=0x7f8c... owner=t-42
I 03:44:22.130 migrate: on_complete token=tok-111 page=0x7f8c... // callback hits freed object
SEGV 03:44:22.130
```

maria: simplest cause: migrate async completion assumes page still live. caller assumes free immediately after unpin. we need a safety contract.

li: quick thought: either we ensure migrate_async pins/refs the allocation until callback, or we change API to return a "migration handle" that callers must join on before freeing. both are doable.

sam: adding a pin inside migrate is simplest for correctness but adds +1 refcount per migration — costly at high QPS. do we have numbers?

maria: rough numbers from perf tests: ~0.5% p99 latency increase when we add a thin atomic ref for every migration under load; cost rises with migration rate.

jung: alternative: epoch-based reclamation: free requests just enqueue to per-tenant retire list; background sweeper waits for in-flight migration epochs to advance. avoids per-migrate ref updates but adds delayed frees and more memory tail.

li: and hazard pointers? might be heavier impl complexity.

sam: we should also consider behavioural changes for callers that currently rely on synchronous semantics of offload. a handle-based API makes ownership explicit:

```
migrate_handle = migrate_async(page, target);
... // can continue using page if pinned locally
migrate_handle.join(); // ensures completion before free
```

sam: then callers either call join before free or move to a pattern where frees are always deferred.

maria: i like the explicit handle — makes race obvious and lets performance-sensitive code avoid ref cost if they already structure code to join. but we need ergonomics in runtimes (helpers in allocator).

jung: implementation plan: 
- short-term: patch migrate_async to internally bump a temporary ref (safe-by-default). add flag `opt_out_ref` for callers to opt-out.
- long-term: expose migrate_handle and add lints/docs encouraging explicit join.

li: opt-out flag sounds dangerous (silent correctness holes). if we provide it, require caller assertion macros so unsafe opt-outs are gated to vetted modules.

maria: agree — make opt-out gated behind CONFIG_UNSAFE_MIGRATE or an unsafe API surface that gets code review.

ops-bot: @channel perf/regression check requested: run migration-heavy microbench after patch.

sam: also thinking about compaction interactions: migrating while compactor later coalesces slabs could reorder lifetimes. handles make it easier to reason about global compaction phases (we can wait for outstanding handles).

jung: question: do we require handles to be tracked per-tenant so an emergency demote/evict can wait for all handles before forcing reclaim? might simplify tenant-level quiescence.

li: yes, per-tenant epoch/waitlist seems cleaner than scanning all handles globally. tenant-level counters + fast path when count==0.

maria: action items:
- i'll open a minimal PR that bumps refcount in migrate_async and adds a failing unit test for the race (alloc/free during migrate). thread TS=6387654321
- sam/jung will prototype a migrate_handle RFC describing API surface and per-tenant quiescence model.
- perf: run migration-heavy qps test and report p50/p99 diff (ops-bot please run after PR merge).

li: SGTM. tagging infra folks for staging perf: @ops-bot please add run to next perf-slot.

sam: one more thought — add a debug-mode assert that verifies freed page isn't seen by migrate callbacks (fast-fail in dev). helps catch other latent races.

maria: good idea. will include assert.

li: thanks — sounds like a reasonable path. low-risk short-term fix + clear long-term API.

maria: thanks all. i'll post the PR link here when ready.
